summary: Verified disk-backed durable persistence fix for StreamClip AI. All 5 pytest tests passed (5/5). Confirmed: (1) POST /api/channels creates channel and writes /app/backend/.appdata/channels.json; (2) After dropping channels collection and restarting backend, GET /api/channels restores 'persist_qa_1' from disk; (3) After writing settings.json snapshot with fake twitch creds, dropping settings collection, and restarting, GET /api/settings returns twitch_configured=true; (4) Regression: /api/demo/seed creates 3 demo channels + 18 clips; /api/settings shape correct with redirect_uri; (5) Cleanup executed - persist_qa_1 deleted, settings collection dropped, settings.json removed, demo re-seeded. Final state: twitch_configured=false, only demo channels (xqc, kaicenat, pokimane).
critical_code_review_comments: restore_from_disk() only restores channels/settings when collections are empty - correct behavior for reset scenarios but won't merge partial data if some channels exist in DB but not disk (or vice-versa). Acceptable for the reported use-case.
channels.json snapshot excludes _id but settings snapshot keeps _id and pops it during restore - inconsistent style but functionally correct.
APPDATA lives under /app which persists in this env; noted in code comment. Good.
seed_data_creation: Demo seed re-invoked at end to leave app in clean baseline state (3 demo channels, 18 demo clips, no twitch config).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Persistence tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_persistence.py. They restart backend twice via supervisorctl and manipulate Mongo directly via pymongo. Tests are idempotent and self-clean. Final baseline: 3 demo channels only, twitch not configured, no settings.json on disk (channels.json regenerated by demo/seed is expected).
